messages.subject: Error from R
parts:
Dear all 

I am fitting a glm in my spatiotemporal data but keep getting errors that I am yet to figure out.

Please, here is my model and I have also attached my data.

Data1<-read.csv("small_subset1.csv")

library(readxl)
library(devtools)
library(foreign)
library(ggplot2)
library(spdep)
library(sp)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(haven)
library(tigris)
library(sf)
library(survey)

tigris::zctas(state = "SC", class = "sf", year = '2010')
zcta_shapefile <- tigris::zctas(state = "SC", class = "sf", year = '2010')
merged_data <- left_join(zcta_shapefile, merged_dataset, by = c("ZCTA5CE10" = "zcta"))

formula1 <-TestResult ~ factor(Ethnicity) + factor(Sex) + factor(Race) +
    factor(AgeatEncounter) + factor(Date) + factor(ZCTA5CE10)
Mod1<-inla(formula1,family="binomial",data=small_subset1,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
           control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),verbose=FALSE)

messages.author: 30b37db3d992e3df
messages.subject: Re: Error from R
parts:
A couple of preliminary points;

1. Your problem has nothing to do with spatial impacts.
Since the problem is reproducible without them, it is
best to include a minimal setup resulting in failure.
Spatiality and all the additional packages are just red 
herrings here.

2. The provided code is wrong: there is no such data
as "small_subset1". I expect that this was a typo: nonetheless,
you really ought to test your code first before posting.

3. You should always post the inla error message. It might
then be obvious to experts just what the problem is.
(Though not, as it happens, in this case).

All that said, I think the actual problem is with your dependent
variable. TestResult is a vector of 1's and 2's. A binomial
model expects 0's and 1's.

The following code seems to work: 

library(INLA)
Data1<-read.csv("small_subset1.csv")
Data1$TR<-Data1$TestResult-1 # transforms 1s into 0s and 2s into 1s

formula1 <-TR ~ factor(Ethnicity) + factor(Sex) + factor(Race) +

(I was a bit surprised that inla call worked without the "required parameter"
Ntrials, with no default, as per binomial.doc. Apparently there is a default.)

Regards,
